question: Examine the system $(k+1)x+2y=4$ and $2(k+1)x+4y=9$. Determine all real values of $k$ for which it is inconsistent.
explanation:
Comparison of the left-hand sides
The left-hand side of the second equation is twice the left-hand side of the first equation for every real value of $k$: $$2[(k+1)x+2y]=2(k+1)x+4y$$
Comparison of constants
If the equations represented the same relation, the constant in the second equation would be $2(4)=8$. However, the given constant is $9$.
Contradictory relations
The equations require the same expression to equal both $8$ and $9$, which is impossible.
Parameter conclusion
Therefore, the system has no solution for every real value of $k$. Hence, it is inconsistent for $$k\in\mathbb{R}$$

options.A: The system is inconsistent only for $k=-1$.
options.B: The system is inconsistent for every $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
options.C: The system is inconsistent only for $k=1$.
options.D: The system is consistent for every $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
